title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt — the annual revision edition, and the only vintage all year that restates prior quarters, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes). The 2027 table's June row reads '30' in the column headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter', under 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'; the note block states 'The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December)'. Corroborated by a SECOND Treasury primary fetched the same session, home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system-home-page/tic-forms-instructions/us-gross-external-debt (HTTP 200, 174,128 bytes), which states the rule in its own words and adds a detail the release-dates page omits: 'Releases are made at 4 PM in Washington D.C. on the last business day of March, June, and September, and at 10 AM on the last business day of December.' PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-09 on the bar tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26 set (one named Treasury primary plus independent mechanical corroboration), with the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching, not the sweep that discovered it. Mechanical corroboration is empirical, not just arithmetic: all 135 archived Table A vintages were fetched from ticdata.treasury.gov and each one's internal 'Source: Department of the Treasury, <date>' stamp read, giving 65 dated publications 2011-2026. The last-business-day rule reproduces 55 of them at offset +0 and 57 within +/-1 day, and 2027-06-30 is a Wednesday and the last business day of June 2027. The four genuine exceptions are informative rather than disqualifying: 2019-01-31 (+31, the 35-day funding lapse), 2024-12-30 (-1), 2026-01-16 (+16, flagged '16 (delayed)' on the release-dates page itself) and 2025-07-02 (+2). THREE OF THE FOUR ARE DECEMBER RELEASES -- the same release the second Treasury page singles out as the 10 AM one. The June sub-series runs 13 of 14 at +0 with one +2. CONFIRMED COVERS THE SCHEDULED DATE AND NOTHING ELSE: the release-dates page carries the standing notice 'When Federal Government offices in Washington D.C. are closed on a release date, that date will be revised after offices reopen'. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26`, now shadowed. WHAT THIS RELEASE IS: the quarterly U.S. gross external debt position as-of 2027-03-31, plus the annual revision that restates the previous calendar year. THE PROPOSER'S RELOCATION CLAIM IS CONFIRMED, AND FAR HARDER THAN IT WAS FILED. It was filed on documentary grounds -- Treasury describes this June release as the survey's one present-tense feedback path. Measured directly from the archive this session: across all 135 archived Table A vintages, 66 of 66 revisions to a previously published quarter carry a JUNE release stamp. Zero March, zero September, zero December, 2012 through 2026. The June edition is not merely the largest revision of the year; it is the only one that exists. BUT THE SURVEY IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT BIG. On the 44 BPM6 vintage pairs where Table A's 'Debt Securities: By Sector' memorandum item is readable, the revision to that item -- the component the Survey of Foreign Holdings could plausibly drive -- explains 2% of the headline revision (regression slope 0.021, correlation 0.132, p=0.40, same-sign 27 of 44, p=0.17). Mean |revision| to debt securities is $43.5bn against $229.3bn for the headline. The June restatement is dominated by loans, deposits and intercompany lending -- the banking-form side -- not by the securities benchmark named in the note. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: 16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is a quarter stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and next-session |delta-10Y| after a June edition is 5.00bp (n=15) against 4.74bp after the other three quarterly editions (p=0.78) -- a null against a perfectly matched control. Nothing here licenses an entry.
